definition: the part of society involved in crime and organized criminal activity

collocations.example: She still has ties to the city's criminal underworld.
Police arrested a notorious underworld figure late last night.

definition: not harmed or injured at all after a dangerous event

collocations.example: The hostages emerged unscathed after their long and frightening ordeal.
She escaped unscathed from the serious car accident on the highway.

definition: to relax after a period of work or tension

collocations.example: Music helps me unwind after a long, busy day at work.
A warm bath helps him unwind before he goes to bed.

definition: cheerful, positive, and full of hope

collocations.example: The team stayed in an upbeat mood despite the narrow loss.
The director gave an upbeat assessment of the project's progress.

definition: the process by which a substance is absorbed or taken in

collocations.example: The drug improves oxygen uptake by the blood during hard exercise.
Healthy soil improves nutrient uptake in young, growing crops.

definition: a young child who is poor, dirty, and often lives on the streets

collocations.example: A hungry street urchin begged for coins near the busy market.
A gang of urchins chased the cart down the narrow alley.

definition: a tool or container, especially one used for cooking or eating

collocations.example: She keeps every kitchen utensil in one neat, tidy drawer.
A wooden spoon is a simple but very useful cooking utensil.

definition: the organ in a woman's body where a baby grows before birth

collocations.example: The fertilized egg implants in the uterus within a few days.
Each month the lining of the uterus thickens and then sheds.

definition: a card or message sent to show love, especially on Valentine's Day

collocations.example: She sent a valentine to her husband every February without fail.
He received an anonymous valentine with no name written inside.

definition: very brave and determined, especially in a difficult situation

collocations.example: They made a valiant effort to save the slowly sinking boat.
The valiant soldiers held the bridge against heavy enemy fire.

definition: the meat from a young cow, called a calf

collocations.example: The restaurant served roast veal with a rich mushroom sauce.
She ordered a breaded veal cutlet with potatoes for dinner.

definition: used to stress that something is really like the strong word used to describe it

collocations.example: The long table held a veritable feast of local dishes.
A veritable army of reporters waited outside the courthouse.

definition: any of the small bones that together form the backbone

collocations.example: He fractured a lumbar vertebra when he fell from the ladder.
The doctor pressed gently on each vertebra along the spine.

definition: a small remaining amount or trace of something that once existed

collocations.example: There was not a vestige of truth in the ugly rumor.
They clung to the last vestige of their old power.

definition: the process of carefully checking someone or something before approval

collocations.example: All new staff must pass a strict security vetting process first.
The documentary went through rigorous vetting before it was released.

definition: a person who is extremely skilled, especially at playing music

collocations.example: The young cellist is already a true virtuoso at nineteen.
He is a virtuoso on the guitar, admired by players worldwide.

definition: (of a disease or poison) extremely dangerous and spreading very quickly

collocations.example: A virulent strain of the flu swept through the small town.
The new virus proved highly virulent and very hard to contain.

definition: based on deep instinct and strong feeling rather than careful thought

collocations.example: The violent film provoked a visceral reaction from the whole audience.
She felt a visceral dislike of the loud, crowded city.

definition: a game in which two teams hit a ball over a high net with their hands

collocations.example: They played beach volleyball all afternoon in the warm sun.
The hotel built a volleyball court right next to the pool.

definition: a crisp cake with a pattern of squares, cooked in a special iron

collocations.example: She poured the thick batter into the hot waffle iron.
He ordered a tall stack of waffles with maple syrup.

definition: an agreement to risk money on the result of an event; a bet

collocations.example: He placed a large wager on the home team to win.
She won a wager with her coworker over the final score.

definition: to allow yourself to enjoy a sad or unpleasant feeling too much

collocations.example: He spent the whole week wallowing in self-pity on the couch.
They wallowed in nostalgia, looking at old photos for hours.

definition: a thin stick used by a magician or believed to have magic powers

collocations.example: She waved her magic wand and the room filled with light.
The fairy touched the pumpkin with her wand.

definition: a crowded maze of narrow passages, streets, or small rooms

collocations.example: The old town was a warren of narrow, winding streets.
The huge hospital was a confusing warren of corridors.

definition: a small, hard growth on the skin caused by a virus

collocations.example: A small wart appeared on the back of his hand.
The doctor used liquid nitrogen to remove the stubborn wart.

definition: having gentle curves; not straight

collocations.example: She has long, wavy hair that falls past her shoulders.
He drew a wavy line to show the winding river.

definition: difficult to control and often behaving badly

collocations.example: The patient teacher struggled to guide the wayward child.
His wayward behavior deeply worried both of his parents.

definition: weapons considered together as a group

collocations.example: The army showed off its modern weaponry at the national parade.
The fortress held an arsenal of weaponry behind its thick walls.

definition: very important and serious

collocations.example: The council debated several weighty matters late into the night.
Leading the whole team is a weighty responsibility for her.

definition: playful or fanciful behavior, ideas, or humor

collocations.example: The garden had a touch of whimsy, with painted gnomes everywhere.
Her children's stories are full of whimsy and gentle humor.

definition: a low, continuous sound made by something turning or moving quickly

collocations.example: He could hear the whir of the vacuum cleaner upstairs.
A faint whir came from the old computer's cooling fan.

definition: happening very fast and involving a lot of activity

collocations.example: After a whirlwind romance, the couple married within just a few weeks.
They took a whirlwind tour of five cities in three days.

definition: to make something smaller or fewer by reducing it gradually

collocations.example: They whittled down the long list of names to just five.
Rising costs slowly whittled away the company's yearly profits.

definition: used to tell someone to stop or slow down, or to show surprise

collocations.example: Whoa, slow down, you are talking way too fast for me.
Whoa, wait a second, that number simply can't be right.

definition: complete and sincere, without any doubt

collocations.example: The new plan was given wholehearted support by the board.
Success requires a wholehearted commitment from every member of the team.

definition: a small door or gate, especially one set into or beside a larger one

collocations.example: She slipped through the wicket gate into the quiet garden.
The old guard opened the wicket to peek at the visitors.

definition: a clever trick used to persuade or deceive someone

collocations.example: She used her feminine wiles to charm the whole committee.
The salesman used every wile he knew to win the contract.

definition: a weak person who is easily frightened or lacks courage

collocations.example: Don't be a wimp; just tell them what you really think.
He felt like a total wimp for backing down so easily.

definition: a machine that pulls or lifts heavy objects using a rope or cable

collocations.example: They used an electric winch to haul the heavy boat ashore.
A worker operated the winch to lower the crates slowly.

definition: based on what you hope for rather than on reality

collocations.example: Hoping for a raise this year is just wishful thinking.
She gave the cake a wishful look before walking away.

definition: a short, sharp cry, especially of pain or surprise

collocations.example: The dog gave a yelp of pain when someone stepped on it.
She let out a yelp when the cold water hit her back.

definition: something that limits your freedom or acts as a heavy burden

collocations.example: The nation finally threw off the yoke of colonial rule.
For years the people lived under the yoke of tyranny.

definition: used to show that something, especially food, tastes very good

collocations.example: Yum, this hot soup is absolutely delicious on a cold day.
Yum, something smells really good in the kitchen right now.

definition: a young professional with a well-paid job and a fashionable lifestyle

collocations.example: He drives a flashy sports car like a typical yuppie.
They enjoyed a comfortable yuppie lifestyle in the city center.

definition: an African wild animal like a horse, with black and white stripes

collocations.example: A herd of zebras grazed calmly on the wide, open plain.
The lion crouched low in the grass to stalk a lone zebra.

definition: a dead body brought back to life in horror stories

collocations.example: The frightened survivors fought off a huge zombie horde.
They stayed up late watching a classic old zombie movie.

definition: extremely bad, hopeless, or without any dignity

collocations.example: Millions of people still live in abject poverty around the world.
The costly project was an abject failure from the very start.

definition: burning strongly; completely on fire

collocations.example: Rioters set several parked cars ablaze during the long night.
The dry field was quickly ablaze after the lightning strike.

definition: the place where someone lives; a home

collocations.example: Welcome to my humble abode; please come inside and sit down.
The man was homeless and had no fixed abode at all.

definition: knowing the most recent facts about something

collocations.example: She reads journals daily to keep abreast of new research.
Good leaders stay abreast of recent developments in their field.

definition: to officially declare that someone is free from blame or guilt

collocations.example: The official report absolved the captain of all blame.
This mistake does not absolve you from responsibility for the error.

definition: the act of formally choosing not to vote

collocations.example: Her abstention from voting surprised the whole committee.
The election saw a high abstention rate among young voters.

definition: a musical instrument played by pulling it in and out and pressing keys

collocations.example: He learned to play the accordion when he was a child.
Lively accordion music filled the small, crowded village square.

definition: a person who uses statistics to calculate insurance risks and costs

collocations.example: She became a qualified actuary after years of difficult exams.
He works as an actuary for a large national insurance firm.

definition: a well-known saying that expresses a general truth

collocations.example: The old adage says that honesty is always the best policy.
As the adage goes, no pain usually means no gain.

definition: the branch of law that deals with ships, shipping, and the sea

collocations.example: Admiralty law governs most legal disputes that happen at sea.
The shipping case was heard in a special court of admiralty.

definition: a word that adds meaning to a verb, adjective, or another adverb

collocations.example: In 'speak quietly,' the word 'quietly' is an adverb of manner.
An adverb usually modifies a verb somewhere in the sentence.

definition: the protection, support, or control of a person or organization

collocations.example: The research continued under the aegis of the large university.
The peace talks proceeded under the aegis of the UN.

definition: to allow air to pass through or mix into something

collocations.example: Careful gardeners aerate the soil so the roots can breathe.
A small pump is used to aerate the water in the tank.

definition: the science or study of building and flying aircraft

collocations.example: She has spent her entire career in the field of aeronautics.
He went to college to study aeronautics and mechanical engineering.

definition: being planned or starting to happen, often secretly

collocations.example: There are plans afoot to build a new library downtown.
Everyone in the office sensed that something strange was afoot.

definition: suddenly filled with shock and horror

collocations.example: She stood aghast at the terrible mess in the kitchen.
He could only stare aghast as the car rolled into the river.

definition: a person who believes we cannot know whether God exists

collocations.example: He has been a committed agnostic for most of his adult life.
She describes herself as an agnostic rather than an atheist.

definition: a sealed room that lets people move between areas of different air pressure

collocations.example: The astronauts passed slowly through the airlock into open space.
He sealed the airlock door before the pressure began to change.

definition: the radio waves used to broadcast radio and television programs

collocations.example: Her catchy new song is finally on the airwaves this week.
Campaign ads filled the airwaves in the weeks before the election.

definition: (of a door or window) slightly open

collocations.example: She left the door ajar so the cat could get out.
The window stood ajar, letting in the cool evening air.

definition: a tree related to the birch that often grows in wet ground

collocations.example: An old alder tree leaned over the quiet, shallow stream.
The simple furniture was made from smooth, pale alder wood.

definition: an elected member of a city or town council

collocations.example: The city alderman promised to fix the broken neighborhood roads.
Voters in the district will elect a new alderman this November.

definition: a false name that someone uses instead of their real name

collocations.example: He checked into the small hotel under an alias.
The famous writer used an alias to protect her privacy.

definition: caring about the needs of others more than your own; unselfish

collocations.example: Helping strangers with no reward is truly altruistic behavior.
Her motives for volunteering were purely altruistic, not selfish.

definition: a mixture or combination of several different things

collocations.example: The popular movie is an amalgam of comedy and horror.
His style is a strange amalgam of old and new ideas.

definition: a medical condition in which someone loses their memory

collocations.example: After the bad crash, he suffered from severe amnesia.
A sudden bout of amnesia erased most of her childhood memories.

definition: a powerful drug that speeds up the nervous system and can be addictive

collocations.example: The clinic treats many patients struggling with amphetamine addiction.
Several athletes have been caught abusing amphetamines before races.

definition: happening or living without the presence of oxygen

collocations.example: Anaerobic bacteria can survive deep underground without any oxygen.
The waste breaks down under anaerobic conditions inside the sealed tank.

definition: something that you strongly dislike or find unacceptable

collocations.example: The idea of censorship is anathema to most honest journalists.
Wasting good food was anathema to my careful grandmother.

definition: a robot designed to look and behave like a human

collocations.example: The film features a humanlike android that can feel real emotion.
Scientists hope to build an android that walks completely naturally.

definition: a small plant with brightly colored, cup-shaped flowers

collocations.example: A delicate wood anemone bloomed in the shady spring forest.
She picked a bunch of purple anemones from the garden.

definition: a strong feeling of worry, anxiety, or unhappiness about life

collocations.example: The honest novel captures the teenage angst of growing up.
His private diary was full of angst about the uncertain future.

definition: to make someone feel angry or hostile toward you

collocations.example: He tried very hard not to antagonize his demanding new boss.
She seemed to deliberately antagonize everyone at the long meeting.

definition: a strong feeling of dislike toward someone or something

collocations.example: He felt a deep antipathy toward dishonest and greedy people.
There was a clear mutual antipathy between the two business rivals.

definition: a person who studies, collects, or sells old and rare objects or books

collocations.example: The noted antiquarian collected rare maps and ancient coins.
As a keen antiquarian, he spent every weekend at antique fairs.

definition: very old-fashioned and no longer suitable for modern use

collocations.example: The struggling factory still relies on antiquated equipment.
Their office computer system is hopelessly antiquated now.

definition: a substance that kills germs and helps prevent infection

collocations.example: The gentle nurse applied antiseptic to the small cut.
She carefully cleaned the wound with a mild antiseptic.

definition: a tiny insect that feeds on the sap of plants and damages crops

collocations.example: An aphid infestation destroyed half of the rose garden.
Hungry ladybugs help farmers control aphids in a natural way.

definition: to divide and share out something among people or groups

collocations.example: The report did not try to apportion blame to anyone.
They agreed to apportion the cost equally among all the owners.

definition: buying something in one market and selling it in another to profit from price differences

collocations.example: Sharp traders quickly spotted an arbitrage opportunity between the two markets.
The fund made millions by engaging in careful currency arbitrage.

definition: known or understood by only a few people; mysterious

collocations.example: The professor shared his arcane knowledge of ancient dead languages.
The tax system is full of arcane rules few people grasp.

definition: a large group of islands close together in the sea

collocations.example: They sailed for weeks to a remote archipelago in the Pacific.
The volcanic archipelago is home to many rare birds.

definition: all the resources or methods available for a particular purpose

collocations.example: Patience is a valuable weapon in any skilled negotiator's armory.
New data tools add greatly to the marketing team's armory.

definition: the use of natural scented oils to improve health and relaxation

collocations.example: She booked an aromatherapy massage to help her relax after work.
He uses lavender aromatherapy oils to help him sleep better.

definition: the use of clever tricks or skill to deceive or create an effect

collocations.example: Her charming, practiced smile was clearly full of artifice.
He spoke plainly and honestly, without any artifice or pretense.

definition: living a very simple, strict life without comfort or pleasure

collocations.example: The quiet monks led an ascetic life far from the city.
His home was remarkably ascetic, with almost no furniture at all.

definition: showing great care, attention, and effort; very hardworking

collocations.example: She was assiduous in checking every detail of the long report.
His assiduous attention to the work impressed everyone in the office.

definition: to make an unpleasant feeling less severe

collocations.example: The mayor tried hard to assuage public fears about the flood.
He sent flowers to assuage his growing feelings of guilt.
